ENDPOINT SURFACE NORMAL MAP (same camera pose and field of view as FINAL VIEW):
Colors encode surface orientation, not object color or distance. RGB channels encode normal components along camera-right (R), camera-up (G), and camera-forward (B): 0 = -1, about 128 = 0, and 255 = +1. Higher R/G/B means a stronger rightward/upward/forward component; a surface facing the camera has low B. Black means missing geometry. Combine this map with START and FINAL VIEW RGB to reason about the final state.

ENDPOINT PANORAMA (360-degree RGB at the FINAL VIEW position):
The panorama is centered on the final camera's facing direction. At mid-height, the center is forward, one-quarter of the width is left, three-quarters is right, and the two joined edges are behind. Top/bottom look up/down; colors are natural RGB, not geometric labels. This is one position, not a sequence of movement frames.
